official_sources.title: GDAL raster scale semantics
official_sources.finding: GetScale returns the multiplier used with offset to convert raw raster values into band units; success must be checked because a default can be returned when metadata is absent.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster offset semantics
official_sources.finding: GetOffset supplies the additive term in physical_value=raw*scale+offset and its success flag distinguishes meaningful metadata from a default.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster unit type
official_sources.finding: GetUnitType may return m, ft, another nonstandard string, or an empty string when unknown; unit identity must not be guessed.

official_sources.title: GDAL RasterIO raw-value behavior
official_sources.finding: RasterIO and ReadBlock do not automatically apply band scale and offset, so raw reads must be decoded explicitly.

official_sources.title: GDAL raw nodata semantics
official_sources.finding: GetNoDataValue returns nodata in the raw storage domain, with no scale or offset applied.

official_sources.title: GDAL nodata success flag
official_sources.finding: The nodata success flag indicates whether a nodata value is actually associated with the band; a returned fallback must not be treated as metadata.

official_sources.title: GDAL Int64 nodata precision
official_sources.finding: Int64 and UInt64 nodata may be lossy through double-valued GetNoDataValue, requiring exact integer nodata APIs when relevant.

official_sources.title: GDAL explicit mask precedence
official_sources.finding: A corresponding external .msk file is used by GetMaskBand before implicit nodata or alpha fallback masks.

official_sources.title: GDAL dataset NODATA_VALUES mask
official_sources.finding: Dataset NODATA_VALUES can generate a per-dataset nodata mask with GMF_NODATA|GMF_PER_DATASET.

official_sources.title: GDAL band nodata mask
official_sources.finding: A band nodata value can generate a mask with GMF_NODATA, excluding raw nodata pixels from analysis.

official_sources.title: GDAL alpha mask semantics
official_sources.finding: When no nodata exists, an applicable UInt8 alpha band may become the mask and is marked GMF_PER_DATASET|GMF_ALPHA.

official_sources.title: GDAL all-valid fallback mask
official_sources.finding: If no explicit mask, nodata, or applicable alpha exists, GDAL returns an all-valid mask with GMF_ALL_VALID.

official_sources.title: GDAL mask flag identity
official_sources.finding: GMF_NODATA and GMF_ALPHA describe distinct validity mechanisms and should not be collapsed into one undocumented rule.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate unscale equation
official_sources.finding: -unscale converts raw scaled values with unscaled_value=scaled_value*scale+offset.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate assigned scale metadata
official_sources.finding: -a_scale assigns scale metadata without modifying pixel values, separating metadata assignment from physical decoding.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate assigned offset metadata
official_sources.finding: -a_offset assigns offset metadata without modifying pixel values, so metadata mutation must not be mistaken for decoded data.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate strict conversion
official_sources.finding: Strict mode can fail on data type conversions that cannot be preserved exactly; lossy conversion is therefore an explicit policy choice.

official_sources.title: GDAL unscale default output dtype
official_sources.finding: gdal raster unscale defaults Byte through Float32 inputs to Float32 output, so decode dtype must be recorded.

official_sources.title: GDAL unscale Float64 retention
official_sources.finding: Float64 input remains Float64 by default during unscale, making source/output precision part of replay identity.

official_sources.title: GDAL unscale metadata absence
official_sources.finding: Bands without scale/offset metadata are left unchanged by gdal raster unscale; absence is not equivalent to asserted scale=1 offset=0 provenance.

official_sources.title: VRT band identity
official_sources.finding: VRTRasterBand carries explicit 1-based band identity and datatype, which must match the terminal elevation band.

official_sources.title: VRT NoDataValue semantics
official_sources.finding: VRT NoDataValue can define reported nodata independently of source nodata and can require explicit source nodata remapping.

official_sources.title: VRT HideNoDataValue semantics
official_sources.finding: HideNoDataValue can conceal a VRT nodata value from readers, so runtime validity cannot rely only on reported metadata without VRT provenance.

official_sources.title: VRT ComplexSource linear scaling
official_sources.finding: ComplexSource can apply ScaleRatio then ScaleOffset to source values, creating derived values that must not be confused with native raw DTM cells.

official_sources.title: VRT ComplexSource source nodata
official_sources.finding: ComplexSource NODATA explicitly controls which source values are treated as nodata during mapping.

official_sources.title: VRT UseMaskBand semantics
official_sources.finding: ComplexSource can use the source mask/alpha through UseMaskBand rather than only a scalar nodata rule.

official_sources.title: VRT LUT and NaN behavior
official_sources.finding: VRT LUT transformations can include NaN as a source key and clamp outside values, making LUT-derived bands unsuitable as unmanifested native elevation sources.

official_sources.title: VRT NoDataFromMaskSource
official_sources.finding: NoDataFromMaskSource can replace source values with nodata based on a mask threshold, so mask-threshold provenance affects validity.

official_sources.title: NumPy finite-value test
official_sources.finding: numpy.isfinite identifies values that are neither NaN nor positive/negative infinity and is suitable for a post-decode finiteness guard.

official_sources.title: NumPy NaN test
official_sources.finding: numpy.isnan distinguishes NaN from infinity under IEEE-754 semantics.

official_sources.title: NumPy infinity test
official_sources.finding: numpy.isinf identifies positive and negative infinity independently of NaN.

official_sources.title: NumPy IEEE-754 nonfinite semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy follows IEEE-754 semantics where NaN and infinity are distinct special floating values.

official_sources.title: NumPy floating machine limits
official_sources.finding: numpy.finfo exposes machine limits for floating dtypes and links to spacing/nextafter for representable-value precision.

official_sources.title: NumPy spacing precision
official_sources.finding: spacing reports distance to the next representable floating value and returns NaN for NaN or infinity, useful for decode precision QA.

official_sources.title: GDAL statistics approximation guard
official_sources.finding: GetStatistics may use overviews or subsets when approximate statistics are allowed, so approximate metadata cannot replace exact terminal extrema reads.

official_sources.title: GDAL overview identity guard
official_sources.finding: Overview selection may return a reduced-resolution band; terminal terrain extrema must remain bound to the intended native band rather than a convenience overview.
